proposals.name: Concrete real-world precedent as evidence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment cites a specific real, named case, company, incident, or historical precedent (not a hypothetical) as direct evidence for its claim, with enough detail to identify it. Score 0 if all evidence is abstract, generic, or purely hypothetical with no named real instance.
proposals.rationale: R55 grounds its objection in the named bankruptcy of Sam Kane Beef Processors LLC as proof a trust doesn't protect sellers; R45 contrasts the proposed control plan against the actual, named Argentine ant eradication program on Santa Cruz Island. Both R55 and R45 are dense_high_card_low, suggesting the dense model rewards this evidentiary move that a checklist scorecard may not specifically probe for.

proposals.name: Explicit engagement with counter-arguments
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies at least one specific objection, trade-off, or opposing consideration to its own position and directly responds to it with reasoning. Score 0 if the comment argues in only one direction and never acknowledges any opposing consideration.
proposals.rationale: R11 explicitly takes on the roe-quality argument for combining pollock seasons and rebuts it with 2019-vs-2020 water-temperature and maturity data; R52 raises and addresses its own worry about needing an AWOS/ASOS alongside its support for the airspace proposal. Both are dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: First-hand operational experience with regulated activity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the commenter describes their own direct, specific experience actually performing or being subject to the regulated activity (e.g., a fisher describing a season they fished, a driver describing using a feature), with concrete operational detail. Score 0 if the comment shows no first-hand experience with the activity, only general or secondhand knowledge.
proposals.rationale: R21 describes the fisher's own participation in the January 2020 voluntary stand-down and its specific dates; R05 describes the commenter's actual day-to-day use of a rearview camera's brightness/contrast controls. Contrast with R08's generic coalition advocacy letter, which contains no first-hand operational account despite being well-organized (dense_low_card_high).

proposals.name: Numbers tied to the rule's specific mechanics
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment supplies numeric figures (percentages, dollar amounts, durations, thresholds) that are explicitly tied to how the specific provision under review operates. Score 0 if the comment contains no such rule-specific numbers, or only generic/unrelated statistics.
proposals.rationale: R31 gives the exact percentages of intersection-event time captured at 15/18.6/20 seconds to justify the EDR recording duration; R11 gives per-zone AFA sideboard limit percentages (Shumagin 0.6047, Chirikof 0.1167, Kodiak 0.2028). Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Identifies unresolved edge case in rule text
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment describes a specific concrete scenario that the proposed rule's text does not clearly address, and explains why the ambiguity matters in practice. Score 0 if the comment raises no such gap or scenario.
proposals.rationale: R01 flags the increasing concentration of outlier payments as something CMS has not analyzed and asks for a specific reconciliation policy; R60 raises the concrete cross-service gap of how Air Force, Army, Navy, and Marine Corps providers with different existing processes will be trained and transitioned. Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Verifiable citation to external primary source
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment cites a specific external study, report, or dataset with enough identifying detail (author/agency, year, and page/section/table) that a reader could locate and check it. Score 0 if the comment cites no external sources, or only vague unattributed appeals like 'studies show'.
proposals.rationale: R45 cites Menke & Holway (2006) and Menke, Fisher, Jetz & Holway (2007) Ecology 88:3164-3175 by name; R24 cites the specific SIGAR report (SIGAR-20-25-SP) with its URL and exact contractor casualty counts (127 vs. 2,214). Both dense_high_card_low, indicating the dense model may reward verifiable sourcing that a checklist scorecard treats no differently from unsupported assertion.

proposals.name: Explicit causal-mechanism / behavioral-response reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment lays out a specific step-by-step causal chain (including, where relevant, how affected parties will change their behavior) connecting the rule to its claimed consequence, rather than merely asserting the consequence. Score 0 if the comment asserts a harm or benefit with no explanation of the mechanism producing it.
proposals.rationale: R55 traces trust requirement -> less money available to dealers -> increased lender risk -> higher borrowing cost -> reduced buying capacity -> lower prices for sellers; R11 explains how a combined season increases lucrative incentive for AFA non-exempt vessels to enter the GOA fishery and why that harms Gulf-dependent boats. Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Self-aware concession about own position's limits
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the commenter explicitly concedes a real limitation, cost, or complication of the position they are advocating for. Score 0 if the comment is purely one-sided advocacy with no self-critical acknowledgment.
proposals.rationale: R01 states 'we agree with the intent to modify the measure... we would instead propose to consider removal' rather than simply rejecting CMS's goal; R52 supports the Class E proposal but flags its own concern that the airport still lacks AWOS/ASOS. Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Precision of the specific action requested
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment specifies an exact, actionable change (specific replacement text, numeric threshold, defined exemption, or concrete step) rather than a vague directional preference. Score 0 if the comment only expresses general support/opposition or says 'please consider' without specifying what should change.
proposals.rationale: R07 proposes specific definitional fixes distinguishing seed sold by count vs. weight; R01 lists numbered, verb-specific asks ('update the base year,' 'develop and implement an outlier reconciliation policy'). Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Identifies a conflated distinction the rule misses
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies two or more meaningfully different sub-cases, categories, or entities that the proposed rule treats identically, and explains the resulting problem. Score 0 if the comment does not draw any such distinction.
proposals.rationale: R07 argues vegetable seed (sold by count) is wrongly folded into rules built for crop seed (sold by weight); R60 argues Air Force's centralized simple-form process, Army's electronic MTF-routed process, and Navy/Marine Corps needs are meaningfully different and shouldn't be handled as one transition. Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Geographic or institutional specificity of third-party impact
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment ties its claimed impact to a specific, named place, community, facility, or institution, with enough detail that the impact could be checked or located. Score 0 if the claimed impact is described only in generic, unlocalized terms (e.g., 'the public', 'the economy').
proposals.rationale: R50 and R57 both describe specific health effects (asthma, cancers) among named neighbors living downwind of auto and steel plants in northeast Ohio tied to the specific SIP provision at issue. Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Constructive alternative offered alongside objection
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if, when opposing a provision, the comment proposes a specific alternative approach that could achieve the agency's underlying goal differently. Score 0 if the comment only rejects the provision with no alternative offered.
proposals.rationale: R01 proposes alternatives to outright rejection, such as further analysis of a three-year rolling average and a new outlier reconciliation policy; R52 pairs support with a specific proposed addition (AWOS/ASOS) rather than simple approval or rejection. Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Direct correction of the agency's own proposal text
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment quotes or closely paraphrases specific language from the proposed rule itself and identifies a specific error, ambiguity, or misstatement in it, explaining the correct reading. Score 0 if the comment does not engage with the specific wording of the proposal at all.
proposals.rationale: R18 quotes the proposed 'uninterrupted power supply' language and asks 'Did you mean Transfer to an Emergency power supply?', explaining the UPS-vs-generator distinction; R54 quotes the proposed Section 401 language and argues it contradicts the Supreme Court's PUD No. 1 v. Washington Dept of Ecology holding, noting the agency relies on the dissent. Both dense_low_card_high, so this criterion tests whether the scorecard's high scores here are picking up genuine textual engagement the dense model underweights.

proposals.name: Concretely described personal stake in the outcome
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the commenter describes a specific, concrete way that they personally (or their household/business) have been or will be affected by the rule or underlying problem, beyond stating an opinion. Score 0 if the comment expresses only a general opinion with no described personal consequence.
proposals.rationale: R10 describes the commenter's house being completely destroyed by the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire and the specific difficulty she had finding submission links despite being an experienced consultant; R50 describes living downwind of auto/steel plants and neighbors developing asthma and cancer. Both dense_high_card_low.

proposals.name: Reconciles the rule against other specific rules or dockets
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment explicitly compares the proposed rule's requirements against another specific, identified rule, docket, airworthiness-directive number, or legal precedent and reasons about consistency between them. Score 0 if the comment treats the rule in isolation with no reference to other specific regulatory provisions.
proposals.rationale: R13 (JAL) directly compares NPRM 2015-NM-169-AD's 24-month compliance window against the 60-month window in AD 2016-04-20 and NPRM 2015-NM-094-AD for the identical part number, and asks for consistency; R51 (DEPA) ties its comments to specific Executive Order 13777 criteria and other named dockets. R13 is dense_low_card_high (0.474/0.998) despite being a short, highly technical cross-reference, suggesting the dense model may undervalue terse but substantively rigorous rule-reconciliation that the scorecard correctly rewards.

proposals.name: Concrete disconfirming instance against the proposal's factual premise
proposals.instruction: Score how far the comment supplies a specific, checkable real-world instance that cuts against a premise the proposed action depends on. 10 = the comment names a particular event, case, program, dataset, or observation (identifiable by name, date, docket, or document) AND states explicitly why that instance contradicts or materially limits the agency's stated premise. 5 = a specific instance is supplied but its bearing on the agency's premise is left for the reader to infer, or the instance is only loosely tied to the premise. 0 = disagreement is carried entirely by opinion, prediction, preference, or generic assertion, with no instance the agency could go look at.
proposals.rationale: R03 defeats the premise of a livestock dealer trust by naming the Sam Kane Beef Processors bankruptcy, where a Packers Trust existed and sellers were still left unpaid; that single named instance does more work than the rest of a very short letter, and it sits at dense_pct=0.652 with card_pct=0.154. R54 does the same to the roe-maturity rationale for combining seasons, using the March 2020 acoustic-trawl survey (2.7 C vs a 3.7 C 40-year average; 92.33% vs 74.72% pre-spawning) — dense 0.854, card 0.176. R35 similarly limits the report's Argentine-ant claim by naming what the published soil-moisture studies do and do not establish. On the other side, R38 and R30 assert impacts with no instance at all and are card-high (0.989, 0.891). A bank that credits 'provides evidence' generically cannot distinguish a decisive counterexample from a decorative fact.

proposals.name: Engages the rule's own preamble, analysis, or cited studies
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment reasons about the agency's own stated basis for the action rather than about the topic in the abstract. 10 = the comment quotes, cites, or accurately restates the agency's reasoning, its regulatory-impact or cost figures, the statutory mandate it is implementing, or the specific studies the preamble relies on, and then argues from that material. 5 = the agency's rationale is gestured at ('the proposal says it will improve safety') without any of its specifics being handled. 0 = the comment never touches the agency's stated reasoning; it argues for or against the policy on general grounds only.
proposals.rationale: R11 (dense 0.895, card 0.380) reconstructs the FAST Act mandate and NHTSA's own duration study before commenting — 5 s at 2 Hz to 20 s at 10 Hz, and the 15 s / 18.6 s / 20 s capture results. R47 (dense 0.902, card 0.311) takes EPA's own cost analysis and nets the roughly $15 million per year of added leakage against the claimed savings of just over $24 million. R18 (dense 0.685, card 0.184) attacks the quality of the epidemiology data used to calibrate and validate EPA's perchlorate model. All three are dense-high/card-low. Card-high rows R30, R36, R31 never touch agency reasoning at all. This is the single most consistent property of the dense_high_card_low half and looks like the clearest thing the bank is missing.

proposals.name: Names a specific omission or missing commitment in the proposal
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies something the proposal fails to say, define, decide, or commit to, at a level of specificity the agency could act on. 10 = the comment points to a particular gap — an unaddressed scenario, an undelivered commitment, an unassigned responsibility, an unanswered question the rule creates — and says what filling it would require. 5 = the comment says the proposal is incomplete or 'falls short' without locating the gap. 0 = the comment engages only what the proposal does say, or offers no gap analysis at all.
proposals.rationale: R58 (dense 0.687, card 0.179) is otherwise campaign-shaped but pins a real omission: the draft lead strategy does not commit to lower acceptable levels for lead-based paint and does not commit to speedy replacement of lead service lines. R25 (dense 0.636, card 0.102) is five sentences long and consists almost entirely of an unassigned-responsibility gap: who trains USAF providers to screen a USMC dependent, and where do the forms go. R32 finds the same kind of hole from the other side (how contingent restitution orders are to be categorized under 6050X). R35 finds it in the science report's pollination biology. Comments that are short and template-flavored can still score very high here, which is exactly where scorecard and dense diverge.

proposals.name: Operator-level implementation path: who does what, with what systems
proposals.instruction: Score how concretely the comment traces what compliance would actually require of the people and systems that must execute it. 10 = the comment describes the existing workflow, equipment, or organizational process in operational detail and shows precisely where the proposal breaks, strains, or is silent about it. 5 = the comment says compliance would be burdensome or infeasible but describes the workflow only in general terms. 0 = no engagement with execution; the comment stays at the level of whether the policy is good or bad.
proposals.rationale: R25 (dense 0.636, card 0.102) contrasts the Air Force's centralized office and simple form against the Army's electronic routing through military treatment facilities, and asks how the Navy and Marine Corps transition. R12 (dense 0.212, card 0.787) is dense-low but shows the shape of the property well: UPS versus generator transfer, bi-annual preventive maintenance and monthly testing, on-the-fly BAS value changes versus offline uploads. R56 (dense 0.826, card 0.292) supplies the same texture from a delivery driver's seat — monitor brightness and contrast controls, interlock interactions, non-backing uses. The dense-high cases pair the operational detail with a decision the agency must make; the card-high ones often supply detail without that hook.

proposals.name: Burden incidence stated together with the mechanism producing it
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment says who specifically gains or bears cost AND by what mechanism, so the incidence claim is inspectable. 10 = named classes of affected party are matched to a stated transmission path (this requirement raises this cost for this actor, which changes this behavior, which lands on this other party). 5 = affected parties are named and costs asserted, but no mechanism links them. 0 = costs or benefits are invoked in the aggregate ('this will hurt the economy') with neither party nor mechanism specified.
proposals.rationale: R13 (dense 0.857, card 0.309) is a plainly written lay comment that nonetheless gets the incidence right: manufacturers who already meet the requirement face no changeover cost, machine operators avoid the separate calorie-declaration cost, and consumers gain the information — three parties, three mechanisms. R16 (dense 0.548, card 0.045) traces a millions-of-dollars PMTA path to the exit of sub-$5-million firms and to market concentration in the incumbents the rule is aimed at. R03 chains a dealer trust to reduced working capital, higher lender risk, contracted financing, reduced buying capacity, and finally to prices received by all livestock sellers. All three are card-low. Card-high R22 and R38 assert economic impact with no mechanism.

proposals.name: Offers an alternative specific enough for the agency to draft
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies a substitute the agency could actually write into the rule. 10 = a concrete alternative with the operative parameters filled in — a threshold, boundary, duration, test, exemption class, or replacement text. 5 = a direction is named ('use a risk-based approach') without the parameters that would let anyone implement it. 0 = the comment only supports or opposes, or asks the agency to 'do more' or 'do better'.
proposals.rationale: R16 (dense 0.548, card 0.045) supplies both the exemption class and the substitute test: exclude firms under $5 million from full PMTA and grant marketing approval on HPHC results. R24 (dense 0.835, card 0.260) supplies eligibility rules — Charter/Headboat operators must show they run charters, General Category boats must meet safety regulations or show a Schedule C. Both are card-low. Note the honest complication: R19 (60 days rather than 30 in proposed section 24.22) and R51 (proposed replacement wording for Special Condition 1) carry the same property and are card-HIGH, dense-low. That contrast suggests the discriminating version of this criterion is an adoptable fix tethered to a harm the commenter has independently established, and the judge should reward that pairing.

proposals.name: Flags an ambiguous term and shows the interpretive consequence
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment isolates a specific word, phrase, or definition in the regulatory text and demonstrates that it admits more than one reading with different practical results. 10 = the term is quoted or cited to its section, at least two readings are laid out, and the divergent consequence of each is stated. 5 = the comment says a term is unclear or asks for a definition without showing what turns on it. 0 = no engagement with the operative text's wording.
proposals.rationale: R01 (dense 0.916, card 0.333) quotes the proposed 201.2(q) definition of coated seed and separately shows that a rule framework built on weight collides with vegetable seed sold by count — a definitional mismatch running through the whole submission. R32 (dense 0.150, card 0.673) lays out both readings of 'ordered to be paid' (the amount at settlement versus the amount actually disbursed years later) and shows they produce different reported figures. R12 and R15 do the same for 'uninterruptible versus emergency power supply', 'not working properly', and 'conventional manufacturer'. This is textual craft that a bank keyed to argument quality or evidence will read as mere nitpicking, yet it is exactly the kind of comment that changes final rule language.

proposals.name: Identifies conflict with another statute, rule, order, or decision
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment locates the proposal against the surrounding legal or regulatory landscape and identifies a specific inconsistency. 10 = a particular other instrument is named (statute section, other rule or AD, court decision, executive order, constitutional provision) and the concrete inconsistency with the proposal is explained. 5 = a general appeal to law, precedent, or 'other agency rules' with nothing named. 0 = the proposal is evaluated in isolation.
proposals.rationale: R50 (dense 0.452, card 0.997) is four sentences and finds a real collision: this NPRM demands the MA30A1017 actuator within 24 months while AD 2016-04-20 and NPRM 2015-NM-094-AD allow 60 months for the same part. R21 and R26 (dense 0.657 / 0.676, card 0.107 / 0.110) both invoke section 110(k)(6) error correction and the claim that EPA acted unlawfully in removing the Air Nuisance Rule without assessing county-level effects — a procedural-legality argument buried inside otherwise campaign-shaped text, which is very likely part of why dense rates those two far above the card. R37 identifies that the proposal contradicts PUD No. 1 v. Washington Dept. of Ecology and leans on that decision's dissent. R39 names the Appointments Clause, the APA, Knight Hawk, and Prairie State.

proposals.name: Position developed through a described, testable deliberative process
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment describes how its position was arrived at across the affected parties it speaks for, in a way a reader could interrogate. 10 = the comment states the process — deliberation among affected parties, reconciliation of divergent sub-interests, explicit coordination with or incorporation of other filings — and shows the position survived that process, including where sub-groups differ. 5 = the comment asserts it speaks for many affected parties but describes no process by which their views were gathered or reconciled. 0 = no indication that the position reflects anything beyond a single unexamined view.
proposals.rationale: R01 (dense 0.916, card 0.333) opens by describing multiple meetings across a broad representation of affected parties to reach consensus, then explicitly flags where sub-sectors diverge (vegetable and conservation seed have different economics from crop seed) rather than papering over it. R60 (dense 0.902, card 0.299) states that it participated in and joins named other submissions, so the agency can treat the filings as one coordinated position. Contrast R20 (dense 0.269, card 0.802), which lists 23 signatory organizations but describes no process at all, and R45 (dense 0.094, card 0.614), which lists coalition members similarly. This is deliberately about described process, not about who the submitter is: the merit signal is that the position has been stress-tested against internal disagreement before it reached the docket.

proposals.name: First-hand fact the record lacks, plus its consequence for the rule
proposals.instruction: Composite. Score the joint presence of (a) a specific fact from direct experience that could not be read off the docket or the proposal, and (b) an explicit consequence drawn from it for a decision the agency must make. 10 = both present and connected: a particular observed practice, local arrangement, timing, or operational reality is reported, and the comment says what the agency should therefore decide differently. 5 = experience is reported vividly but yields only a general endorsement, objection, or appeal to trust the commenter. 0 = experience is asserted as standing alone ('I have worked in this field for decades') with no fact and no consequence.
proposals.rationale: R23 (dense 0.789, card 0.143) reports that descendants of an individual land grant hold and use resources as small sole proprietorships, and then draws the consequence: FEMA's definition of 'business loss' will likely fail to recognize them. R54 (dense 0.854, card 0.176) reports the January-February 2020 voluntary stand-down and draws the consequence that a larger combined-season fleet cannot coordinate one, driving Chinook bycatch. R56 (dense 0.826, card 0.292) reports that rear cameras are used in non-backing maneuvers and that monitors have brightness controls, and draws the consequence for the timeout requirement. The failing side is instructive: R06 (dense 0.238, card 0.785) has 30-plus years of permit-holder experience and R43 has 100,000 members' worth of professional standing, but both convert that standing mainly into general endorsement. The scorecard appears to credit the experience; dense appears to credit only experience that pays out in a fact.

proposals.name: Actionable procedural request with a reason tied to the record
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment asks the agency to do something procedural that is within its power, with a stated reason. 10 = a specific procedural action is requested — extend or reopen the comment period, defer action pending analysis, phase the effective date, re-notice, publish a tracking or timeline commitment — with a stated reason grounded in the record or in the requester's circumstances. 5 = process is criticized but no request is made, or a request is made with no reason. 0 = no procedural dimension.
proposals.rationale: R57 (dense 0.932, card 0.399) is the sharpest case in the slice: it does almost nothing except request a 60-day extension so that comments can be completed, and dense puts it in the top 7 percent while the card puts it in the bottom 40. R24 (dense 0.835, card 0.260) makes the same move with a reason the agency could not have supplied itself — that soliciting comment at the height of the summer fishing season excludes the people on the water daily from June through October. R14 asks for an application status tracking system with published review timelines. A procedural ask is cheap to grant and directly changes the proceeding, which is plausibly why the dense model weights it and a merit-of-argument bank does not.

proposals.name: Calibrated partial agreement that isolates exactly the disputed provision
proposals.instruction: Score how precisely the comment separates what it accepts from what it disputes. 10 = the comment explicitly endorses identified parts of the proposal (including its goal or the reasoning behind it) and then localizes its objection to a named provision, parameter, or subset of cases, so the agency can see the minimal change requested. 5 = a general 'I support this but' with the objection left diffuse. 0 = undifferentiated support or undifferentiated opposition to the whole action.
proposals.rationale: R04 (dense 0.758, card 0.267) endorses the Class E designation and calls the 6.4-mile radius reasonable, then localizes: add AWOS/ASOS for METARs, and examine the interaction with operations at the neighboring Class C at GRR. R18 (dense 0.685, card 0.184) agrees that extending the model into early pregnancy captures a genuinely vulnerable window, and disputes only the quality of the data used to do it. R01 accepts the integration effort in principle and objects to the count-versus-weight consequences. R27 shows the same discipline from the card-high side. Contrast the undifferentiated R33 and R30. Calibrated concession is what makes a comment usable in a final-rule response, and it is easy for a bank to score as weak advocacy.

proposals.name: Load-bearing quantities that are sourced and checkable
proposals.instruction: Score whether the numbers in the comment carry the argument and can be verified. 10 = quantities appear with units and a traceable source (named study, report, table, page, docket, or the commenter's own recorded operations), and removing them would collapse the argument. 5 = numbers are present and relevant but unsourced, or sourced but decorative. 0 = no quantities, or quantities that are unsourced and merely rhetorical.
proposals.rationale: R54 (dense 0.854, card 0.176) cites the AFA Review Document at page 174, Table 17, gives GOA non-exempt sideboard limits to four decimals, and contrasts 2.7 C against a 40-year 3.7 C average and 92.33% against 74.72% pre-spawning — every number is doing work. R11 (dense 0.895, card 0.380) reproduces NHTSA's 2 Hz to 10 Hz and 50/90/99 percent capture figures from the agency's own study. R29 sets 127 recorded SPOT deaths against 2,214 conservatively identified by SIGAR with the report linked. The over-credit direction is visible too: R31 (card 0.998) quotes an unnamed 'report' and R46 (card 0.644) asserts one million animals killed per day with no source, and both are scored high by the card. Presence of numbers or of a quotation appears to be rewarded where sourcing and load-bearing-ness are not.

proposals.name: Anticipates and answers the strongest contrary rationale
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment engages the best argument on the other side rather than only its own. 10 = the comment states the opposing rationale (the agency's, another commenter's, or the obvious objection) accurately and in its strongest form, then answers it on its own terms. 5 = an opposing point is acknowledged and waved off without an answer. 0 = the comment argues one side only, as if no reasonable contrary view existed.
proposals.rationale: R54 (dense 0.854, card 0.176) explicitly raises the roe-quality argument made by other commenters, grants that maturity has run early in recent years, and answers it with evidence that the temperature anomaly is reverting. R56 (dense 0.826, card 0.292) states the distraction objection attributed to manufacturers and answers it with the brightness and screen-off controls. R47 takes the proposal's own economic-benefit case and nets the added leakage cost against the claimed savings. R10 (dense 0.769, card 0.224) concedes outright that increasing security reduces liberty before arguing why the tradeoff is acceptable for classified enterprise data. The card-high rows R38, R31, R55 are one-sided throughout, and R38 in particular reads as a talking-points list with no opposing view in view at all.

proposals.name: Every claim bears on a decision this rulemaking must make
proposals.instruction: Score the fraction of the comment's substantive content that is responsive to the question actually before the agency in this proceeding. 10 = every claim and request maps to a determination the agency has to make in this action; nothing is adjacent policy grievance or expressive material. 5 = a responsive core surrounded by substantial off-question material, or a responsive position argued mostly through unrelated concerns. 0 = the comment is about a different policy question, or is expressive or rhetorical without a request the agency could act on in this docket.
proposals.rationale: This is the clearest over-credit direction in the slice. R31 sits at card_pct=0.998 — the top of the bank — while arguing in a harvest-specifications docket that offshore wind should be banned, which is not a determination before that agency in that action. R36 (card 0.933) is a poem about losing a home to wildfire, with real emotional force and no request. R30 (card 0.891) is a single garbled line of product endorsement. R42 (dense 0.722, card 0.092) fails the same test from the other side by recasting color standards for carrots as an epochal shift in the agricultural economy. High-end anchors are R32, R50, and R12, where every paragraph lands on something the agency has to resolve. A bank that rewards vividness, quotation, stated stake, or clear position independently of responsiveness will systematically overrate the R31/R36/R30 family.

proposals.name: Rule-text anchoring
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment pinpoints multiple proposed provisions and explains their operation; score 0 when it offers only generic policy sentiment without engaging the proposal.
proposals.rationale: R18, R40, and R57 engage specific technical provisions, whereas R29 and R53 largely express support or opposition without analyzing rule text.

proposals.name: Actionable amendment precision
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies precise replacement language, thresholds, definitions, procedures, or parameters; score 0 when the requested action is only “do more,” “act quickly,” or approval/rejection.
proposals.rationale: R26 proposes text and justification, R41 requests clarification of a specific phrase, and R47 identifies a precise compliance-period change; R10 and R53 remain broadly directive.

proposals.name: Causal mechanism from rule to consequence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces a credible step-by-step mechanism from the proposed requirement to concrete effects; score 0 when it merely asserts that the rule is good or harmful.
proposals.rationale: R37 explains how combining seasons changes participation, timing, and bycatch, while R60 connects a trust to financing and market effects; R44 mostly predicts broad economic importance without a mechanism.

proposals.name: Traceable, relevant evidence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when claims are supported by identifiable studies, records, measurements, or data directly relevant to the proposal; score 0 when claims rely only on unsupported assertion or rhetoric.
proposals.rationale: R18 cites experimental studies tied to invasion mechanisms, R22 scrutinizes epidemiological inputs, and R50 references a study’s limited scope; R08 and R33 provide essentially no verifiable support.

proposals.name: Evidence critique and uncertainty calibration
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes strong evidence from weak evidence, identifies assumptions or limitations, and calibrates confidence; score 0 when it treats all claims as certain or ignores contrary evidence.
proposals.rationale: R18 identifies missing biological research and limits of extrapolation, R22 questions model-data quality, and R37 distinguishes observed trends from uncertain long-term patterns; R20 presents many consequential claims without comparable qualification.

proposals.name: Quantified impact and baseline comparison
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment quantifies effects and compares them with a baseline, alternative, or relevant historical level; score 0 when impacts are described only with vague intensifiers.
proposals.rationale: R04 uses capture percentages to justify a recording duration, R24 quantifies savings and leakage costs, and R37 compares catch, temperature, and maturity data; R30 and R53 mostly use unquantified urgency.

proposals.name: Feasible implementation pathway
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains who must act, what systems or resources are required, how transition occurs, and how timing is managed; score 0 when it requests a result without an implementation path.
proposals.rationale: R17 identifies cross-service training and responsibility gaps, R55 proposes status tracking and timelines, and R57 specifies testing and documentation practices; R10 asks for deadlines without explaining execution.

proposals.name: Failure-mode and edge-case analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment examines foreseeable failure conditions, unusual operating contexts, secondary effects, and safeguards; score 0 when it discusses only normal or ideal operation.
proposals.rationale: R57 analyzes power-transfer, airflow-reversal, and control-system failures, R27 identifies night-driving and delivery-operation issues, and R09 describes nighttime UAS safeguards; R31 offers no comparable operational analysis.

proposals.name: Cross-rule and system consistency
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies interactions, conflicts, duplicated requirements, or coordination needs across related rules, agencies, or workflows; score 0 when it treats the proposal in isolation.
proposals.rationale: R47 compares overlapping aircraft directives, R59 addresses conflicting product classifications, and R50 distinguishes risks across tax forms; R39 notes neighboring airspace but develops the interaction only partially.

proposals.name: Legal authority and interpretive fit
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accurately connects the proposal to statutory language, delegated authority, precedent, or applicable legal limits; score 0 when legal conclusions are asserted without textual or doctrinal support.
proposals.rationale: R42 invokes and applies Supreme Court interpretation, R28 analyzes statutory authority and rulemaking requirements, and R56 connects discretion to constitutional and APA concerns; R15 raises legal objections but leaves them largely unspecified.

proposals.name: Distributional incidence and equity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which populations, firms, places, or users bear distinct costs and benefits and explains unequal exposure or access; score 0 when effects are described only for an undifferentiated public.
proposals.rationale: R07 explains how reimbursement affects older Medicare patients’ access, R20 connects vaccine access to children and immunocompromised households, and R30 identifies lead burdens in vulnerable communities; R44 discusses consumers and producers only abstractly.

proposals.name: Dynamic and long-horizon consequences
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment addresses timing, transition, behavioral adaptation, cumulative effects, or consequences unfolding over years; score 0 when it considers only an immediate static effect.
proposals.rationale: R32 discusses monitoring and habitat management over decades, R37 analyzes seasonal timing and changing ocean conditions, and R55 addresses long-lived infrastructure; R36 mainly asserts future growth without analyzing its dynamics.

proposals.name: Monitoring, verification, and feedback design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes measurable indicators, data collection, verification methods, reporting, or triggers for revisiting the approach; score 0 when it offers no way to test or track performance.
proposals.rationale: R16 calls for complete public casualty data, R32 requires sustained monitoring with funding, R40 warns that unreliable coding corrupts later analysis, and R57 specifies acceptable verification evidence; R53 supplies no measurement framework.

proposals.name: Context-specific knowledge made generalizable
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when concrete observations from an affected setting are translated into implications that could guide a broadly applicable rule; score 0 when personal or local experience is reported without regulatory analysis.
proposals.rationale: R14 links fishing-season realities to allocation and participation rules, R21 explains prairie management practices in relation to exceptional-event criteria, and R39 connects local airport operations to airspace design; R29 mainly reports positive service experience.

proposals.name: Counterargument and tradeoff handling
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment recognizes serious competing objectives or objections, compares them explicitly, and explains why its recommended balance is preferable; score 0 when it relies on one-sided advocacy without addressing tradeoffs.
proposals.rationale: R19 weighs security against liberty, R21 weighs prescribed-fire benefits against smoke concerns, R24 weighs compliance savings against leakage costs, and R60 weighs risk reduction against financing and market effects.

proposals.name: Rule-text pinpointing
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies an exact proposed provision and specifies a concrete revision; score 0 when it only expresses support or opposition without an identifiable rule-text target.
proposals.rationale: R17 pinpoints conflicting compliance deadlines, while R03 requests a broader boundary without analyzing specific proposed language.

proposals.name: Mechanistic causal chain
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces a plausible sequence from the proposal through behavior or implementation to specific consequences; score 0 when it merely asserts that the proposal will help or harm.
proposals.rationale: R13 explains how a statutory trust could affect lending, dealer capacity, and livestock prices, whereas R19 largely asserts economic and social harm without intermediate mechanisms.

proposals.name: Evidence traceability
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when claims are supported by identifiable studies, datasets, records, or quantified observations interpreted as relevant to the proposal; score 0 when claims are unsupported or rely only on broad assertions.
proposals.rationale: R14 cites published invasion studies and explains their limits, while R25 names possible offshore-wind effects without supplying traceable supporting evidence.

proposals.name: Uncertainty calibration
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment clearly separates established facts, inferences, assumptions, and unresolved uncertainty; score 0 when it presents speculation or contested claims as certain.
proposals.rationale: R14 distinguishes documented findings from prediction difficulties, while R41 shifts among strong assertions, personal worries, and uncertainty without a stable evidentiary boundary.

proposals.name: Feasible alternative design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment offers an implementable alternative, exception, threshold, or safeguard and explains how it preserves the proposal’s legitimate objective; score 0 when it offers only approval, rejection, or an unelaborated demand.
proposals.rationale: R07 proposes specific testing and documentation distinctions, and R59 suggests status tracking and an additional criterion; both contrast with comments offering only broad positions such as R25.

proposals.name: Operational implementability
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies responsible actors, workflows, training, system dependencies, or failure modes that determine whether the rule can work in practice; score 0 when implementation is treated as automatic.
proposals.rationale: R07 analyzes HVAC, power-transfer, testing, and alarm workflows, while R44 asks who will train providers and route forms across military services.

proposals.name: Edge-case coverage
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies materially different contexts or affected populations and explains why the proposed approach may operate differently in each; score 0 when it assumes a homogeneous setting.
proposals.rationale: R06 distinguishes workers by age and disability, and R38 identifies different radiopharmaceutical settings, products, and patient-access conditions.

proposals.name: Tradeoff accounting
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment weighs competing benefits, costs, risks, and affected parties with an explicit comparison; score 0 when it presents only one-sided benefits, harms, or political preferences.
proposals.rationale: R13 compares risk reduction against financing and market effects, while R48 weighs compliance savings against leakage and climate consequences.

proposals.name: Empirical evaluation plan
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes measurable data collection, testing, monitoring, benchmarks, or validation procedures tied to a decision; score 0 when it merely calls for more study or oversight.
proposals.rationale: R07 specifies failure testing and acceptable documentation, while R36 calls for systematic collection, analysis, and public disclosure of contractor casualty data.

proposals.name: Temporal transition reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment analyzes timing, sequencing, phase-in, duration, seasonal variation, or changing conditions and connects them to the rule’s effects; score 0 when timing is ignored.
proposals.rationale: R17 identifies conflicting 24- and 60-month compliance periods, and R18 explains how season timing, temperature, and fish movement affect bycatch and participation.

proposals.name: Interaction and spillovers
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces consequences across connected systems, actors, jurisdictions, or environmental processes, including meaningful second-order effects; score 0 when it considers only the immediate direct effect.
proposals.rationale: R18 connects season consolidation to vessel participation, fishing timing, quota use, and Chinook bycatch, while R28 links roads and corridors to migration, collisions, genetics, and climate adaptation.

proposals.name: Generalized firsthand evidence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when personal experience supplies concrete observations and is translated into a rule-relevant, potentially generalizable pattern; score 0 when it is only anecdote, praise, or emotion without analyzable detail.
proposals.rationale: R01 connects lived exposure to pollution with specific accountability and air-quality mechanisms, whereas R05 provides positive travel experience without evidence about the regulatory question.

proposals.name: Legal textual reasoning
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies governing statutory, regulatory, or precedential language and applies it directly to the proposal; score 0 when it states a legal conclusion without textual reasoning.
proposals.rationale: R34 invokes and applies a specific Supreme Court interpretation of Clean Water Act authority, while R46 raises constitutional and administrative-law concerns but provides less direct application in the excerpt.

proposals.name: Scope prioritization
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment separates the central issue from tangents, ranks its recommendations, and gives a decision-ready conclusion; score 0 when it is diffuse, internally unfocused, or consists mainly of generic requests.
proposals.rationale: R45 isolates a precise reporting ambiguity and asks a focused interpretive question, while R49 lists broad review goals without prioritizing a concrete regulatory decision.

proposals.name: Distributional impact specificity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which groups bear particular risks or receive particular benefits and explains the concrete exposure or allocation mechanism; score 0 when it invokes the public, communities, jobs, or fairness only in generic terms.
proposals.rationale: R24 identifies children, households, schools, lead-pipe users, and multiple exposure pathways, while R19 mentions businesses and food-dependent customers without specifying how impacts are distributed.

proposals.name: First-hand operational knowledge revealing regulatory blind spots
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the commenter draws on direct, sustained personal experience operating within the regulated system and uses that experience to surface a specific factual dynamic the agency appears unaware of (e.g., how actors actually behave under the rule, a practical constraint the rule ignores). Score 0 if the comment offers no experiential insight or merely asserts authority without conveying operational detail.
proposals.rationale: R03 is a 30-year fisherman explaining exactly how combining A&B seasons would undermine voluntary bycatch stand-downs—a dynamic no landlocked analyst would invent. R14 similarly explains that soliciting comments during peak fishing season systematically excludes the most affected stakeholders. R39 reveals that Air Force and Navy use entirely different dependent-screening processes, making a one-size-fits-all rule unworkable. The scorecard likely has no criterion for tacit practitioner knowledge that fills an information gap in the agency's model.

proposals.name: Quantitative specificity grounding the argument
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment embeds specific, verifiable numbers—percentages, dollar amounts, temperature readings, catch rates, citation counts—that directly support its policy position, not merely as decoration. Score 0 if the comment is purely qualitative or uses round-number estimates without sourcing.
proposals.rationale: R03 cites exact sideboard limits (0.6047, 0.1167, 0.2028), average catch rates (26.5%), and water-temperature survey data (2.7°C vs. 3.7°C 40-year average) to rebut the agency's roe-quality rationale. R54 marshals NHTSA's own study findings (15 seconds = 50% capture, 18.6 = 90%, 20 = 99%) to evaluate the proposed recording duration. The dense model likely perceives that quantitative density signals the commenter has done homework the agency must engage with.

proposals.name: Unintended-consequence argumentation
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies a causal pathway by which the proposed rule, if adopted, would produce an outcome diametrically opposed to its stated purpose—and traces that pathway with specific steps. Score 0 if the comment simply states the rule is 'bad' or 'harmful' without explaining the perverse mechanism.
proposals.rationale: R35 argues a livestock dealer trust would reduce money available for livestock purchases and increase lender risk, thereby depressing market prices for the very sellers the trust purports to protect. R38 argues the PMTA process's cost will eliminate small vape businesses and consolidate the market into Big Tobacco—the companies most attractive to youth. R03 shows that combining seasons to improve efficiency would actually increase Chinook bycatch by making voluntary stand-downs impossible. This form of reasoning—'your cure causes the disease'—is high-value regulatory input that a checklist may not isolate.

proposals.name: Actionable alternative proposal with stated mechanism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment proposes a specific, implementable alternative to the proposed rule (or a specific modification) AND explains the causal mechanism by which the alternative would work better. Score 0 if the comment only opposes, only supports, or proposes an alternative so vague it cannot be operationalized.
proposals.rationale: R38 doesn't just oppose PMTAs—it proposes excluding businesses under $5M and substituting HPHC testing as the approval pathway, with a clear logic. R32 proposes adding AWOS/ASOS weather reporting as a safety complement to the Class E airspace designation. R02 recommends a specific additional scoring criterion for engineered projects that deliver environmental co-benefits. The scorecard may credit 'suggests an alternative' generically, but the dense model appears to weigh whether the alternative is concretely operational and mechanistically justified.

proposals.name: Preemptive rebuttal of agency's own stated rationale
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies the specific reasoning the agency gave in the NPRM or preamble for a proposal and then directly counters that reasoning with evidence or logic, not merely asserting disagreement. Score 0 if the comment states a position without engaging the agency's justification.
proposals.rationale: R03 explicitly addresses the argument that combining seasons would improve roe quality, then rebuts it with 2020 survey data showing 92.33% pre-spawning status and water temperatures trending back to normal. R56 engages EPA's cost-benefit analysis line by line, showing the 'savings' are offset by $15M in additional leak costs. R43 systematically addresses EPA's authority arguments under the Clean Air Act. This head-on engagement with the agency's actual logic is distinct from generic opposition.

proposals.name: Expert methodological critique of data or analytical sufficiency
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment, drawing on domain expertise, identifies a specific methodological weakness in the data, model, or analysis underlying the proposal—e.g., a data source is unreliable, a sample is biased, a model omits a key variable. Score 0 if the comment does not engage the agency's analytical basis.
proposals.rationale: R33 is a 20-year Argentine ant researcher who identifies that the Species Report misrepresents invasion risk by ignoring how urban development changes soil moisture in unpredictable ways, and cites an additional peer-reviewed paper the report omitted. R55 critiques the epidemiology data underpinning the perchlorate model, questioning data quality in early pregnancy. R37 explains why police officers cannot reliably code vehicle automation level at crash scenes—identifying a measurement-validity problem the agency overlooked.

proposals.name: Causal mechanism chain connecting rule to outcome
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment traces a multi-step causal chain (A → B → C → D) showing precisely how the proposed rule would lead to a specific outcome, with each link specified. Score 0 if the comment asserts outcomes without connecting the intermediate steps.
proposals.rationale: R03 traces: combining seasons → more AFA vessels participate → voluntary stand-down becomes impossible → Chinook bycatch increases → fall fishery harmed. R38 traces: PMTA cost → small business exit → Big Tobacco monopoly → youth-attractive products dominate → youth vaping increases. This explicit step-by-step mechanism is more probative than asserting 'this will be bad for small business' and appears to be something the dense model rewards.

proposals.name: Lived experience anchored to specific regulatory provision
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment weaves together a first-person account of direct personal impact WITH citation to or engagement with a specific provision, section, or legal standard of the proposed rule—showing exactly where the rule fails the lived reality. Score 0 if the comment describes personal hardship but never ties it to regulatory text, or cites text without any experiential grounding.
proposals.rationale: R16 describes neighbors developing asthma and cancer near steel plants, then anchors that experience to the specific SIP removal, the 110(k)(6) error-correction provision, and the county-level effect analysis EPA failed to conduct. R51 describes being a fire victim, then ties her experience to specific paragraphs of FEMA's proposed rule on allowable damages and attorney fees, identifying where the rule conflicts with New Mexico tort law. The scorecard may credit either personal narrative or legal citation separately, but the dense model appears to value their integration.

proposals.name: Implementation feasibility analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies specific practical barriers to implementing the rule as written—systems that don't exist, data that can't be collected, transitions that can't be executed—and explains why. Score 0 if the comment does not address whether the rule can actually be operationalized.
proposals.rationale: R39 asks who will train USAF providers to conduct screenings they've never done, how centralized and electronic systems will transition, and who ensures all facilities can comply. R36 raises detailed implementation questions about biosafety failure testing—what documentation proves no airflow reversal, which HVAC components require testing, how to handle minor vs. major programming changes. R04 notes that some vehicles lack the timeout feature the rule assumes and describes unique FedEx operational scenarios the rule may disrupt.

proposals.name: Distributional analysis of winners and losers
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies specific, named groups that would differentially benefit or be harmed by the rule and explains the mechanism of the differential impact with specificity. Score 0 if the comment refers to generic 'stakeholders' or 'the public' without distinguishing among affected groups.
proposals.rationale: R03 identifies Gulf-dependent boats without alternative fisheries as the losers and AFA non-exempt vessels with rationalized Bering Sea quota as the winners from season combination. R35 traces how a livestock dealer trust would hurt lenders (increased risk), small dealers (reduced buying capacity), and ultimately sellers (lower prices). R56 notes the rollback creates winners (non-compliant companies) and losers (companies already investing in leak repair), distorting the competitive landscape.

proposals.name: Temporal, seasonal, or sequencing analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment explains why the timing, sequencing, seasonal placement, or phase-in schedule of the rule matters and identifies a specific temporal problem. Score 0 if the comment treats the rule as temporally neutral or only mentions timing in passing.
proposals.rationale: R03's entire argument hinges on the seasonal break between A and B seasons as a bycatch control mechanism—removing it changes the fleet's fishing pattern at a biologically critical time. R14 argues that the comment period itself is mistimed because it falls during the peak fishing season when affected stakeholders are on the water. R44 argues that 5-year permit cycles don't align with long-term marine mammal research programs that extend beyond permit duration, creating wasteful restart cycles.

proposals.name: Definitional or categorizational gap identification
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment identifies a specific term, category boundary, or classification in the proposed rule that is ambiguous, circular, or fails to capture a real-world distinction the commenter can articulate. Score 0 if the comment does not engage with how the rule defines or categorizes anything.
proposals.rationale: R06 identifies that 'ordered to be paid' is ambiguous for contingent restitution orders—does it mean the amount ordered at settlement or the amount actually disbursed years later? R33 shows the Species Report's buffer concept fails to account for how development changes soil moisture categorically. R37 argues that 'level of automation' is not a reliably codeable category given that features are software-enabled and invisible to inspection. The dense model may perceive that definitional precision is a form of regulatory craftsmanship the scorecard doesn't explicitly reward.

proposals.name: Novel factual contribution to the record
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment introduces specific information—a data point, a real-world event, an unpublished observation, a local condition—that is plausibly not already in the agency's administrative record and is relevant to the rule. Score 0 if the comment only reiterates information already in the NPRM or offers pure opinion.
proposals.rationale: R03 contributes 2020 acoustic trawl survey preliminary results (water temperature, maturity composition) that postdate or may not have been in the agency's analysis. R45 introduces SIGAR's audit findings showing the SPOT database undercounted contractor deaths by a factor of 17 (127 vs. 2,214). R51 contributes specific information about how land-grant resource sharing works in northern New Mexico—a cultural-institutional fact FEMA's framework doesn't account for. Novel facts force the agency to respond under APA obligations.

proposals.name: Reasoning from analogous precedent or comparator case
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment draws a specific, well-specified analogy to another regulatory program, prior agency action, or parallel situation and extracts a transferable lesson. Score 0 if the comment makes no comparative argument or draws an analogy too loose to be instructive.
proposals.rationale: R42 argues by direct analogy: CMS already pays solid-organ acquisition costs separately from the bundled payment, and the same logic should apply to bone marrow and cord blood transplants. R43 argues the 2012 Rule's incorporation of transmission and storage into the production source category was unprecedented and should be reversed. R51 compares FEMA's current approach unfavorably to the Cerro Grande Fire process, showing where the agency deviated from its own prior practice. Comparator reasoning gives the agency a concrete model to evaluate against.

proposals.name: Internal logical coherence of the full argument
proposals.instruction: Score 10 if the comment's points fit together as a single integrated argument—each claim supports the others, there are no internal contradictions, and the conclusion follows from the premises. Score 0 if the comment is a list of disjointed points, contains self-contradictory claims, or reaches conclusions not supported by its own evidence.
proposals.rationale: R03 is exemplary: the sideboard data, the AFA participation incentive, the bycatch-stand-down mechanism, the roe-quality rebuttal, and the water-temperature data all converge on a single integrated conclusion. By contrast, R22 (dense_low_card_high) is eloquent but its poetic observation about a 'burning crew' doesn't connect to any regulatory proposition. R05 (dense_low_card_high) quotes a report about offshore wind impacts but never connects that to the harvest specifications being commented on. The dense model appears to perceive structural coherence that the scorecard's item-by-item scoring cannot capture.

proposals.name: Lived-experience-to-mechanism linkage
proposals.instruction: Score whether the author's direct personal or professional experience is used not merely as emotional color but as evidence about how a specific regulatory mechanism actually operates or would operate. A 10 means the experience is concrete, credible, and tightly connected to a specific provision or process—e.g., 'I fish these waters and here is exactly how the proposed season change would alter bycatch patterns.' A 0 means no personal or professional experience is offered, or experience is mentioned but never connected to any regulatory mechanism.
proposals.rationale: The dense model appears to reward experience-grounded reasoning that the scorecard may not distinguish from generic advocacy. R02 connects living downwind from steel plants to the Air Nuisance Rule's enforcement utility, and R07 draws on daily driving to explain exactly when camera displays help or distract—both dense-high. By contrast, R54 offers a visceral wildfire poem with no regulatory mechanism, and R53 asserts medical credentials without showing how they bear on the rule—both dense-low despite card-high scores.

proposals.name: Cascading consequence chain
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment traces a specific multi-step causal chain showing how the proposed rule would produce effects beyond its intended scope, with each link being concrete and plausible rather than speculative. A 10 means at least three linked causal steps, each with a specific mechanism named (e.g., cost increase → small-firm exit → market concentration → reduced competition → higher consumer prices). A 0 means no causal chain is articulated, or only a single-step assertion of harm or benefit.
proposals.rationale: R08 (dense 0.548) traces PMTA compliance costs → small-business failure → Big Tobacco monopoly → reduced public-health outcomes, a multi-step chain the scorecard (0.045) misses entirely. R38 (dense 0.789) links season consolidation → increased AFA participation → breakdown of voluntary stand-down agreements → elevated Chinook bycatch. Dense-low comments like R59 and R60 assert outcomes ('would be substantial,' 'should be banned') without articulating the intermediate causal steps.

proposals.name: Regulatory design critique with alternative
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a structural flaw in how the regulation is designed—its scope, incentives, thresholds, or architecture—and proposes a specific alternative mechanism, not merely opposing or supporting the proposal. A 10 means the comment both diagnoses a design problem and offers a concrete, workable alternative with rationale. A 0 means the comment takes a position (support or oppose) but offers no analysis of regulatory design.
proposals.rationale: R08 proposes tiered HPHC testing keyed to business size as an alternative to uniform PMTA requirements, diagnosing the structural problem of cost-prohibitive compliance. R50 (dense 0.857) analyzes why the labeling rule's design benefits all three stakeholder groups and proposes it as superior to alternatives. Dense-low R11 simply opposes removal of SOE from the National List without any design analysis, and R10 asks for parity with solid-organ reimbursement without examining why the current design differs.

proposals.name: Quantitative evidence with analytical integration
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment presents specific numbers, data, or quantitative comparisons and explicitly explains what those numbers mean for the rule's design or impact. A 10 means multiple data points are woven into a coherent analytical argument where each number does interpretive work. A 0 means no quantitative content, or numbers are dropped in without being connected to any argument about the rule.
proposals.rationale: R38 integrates sideboard limits, historical catch percentages, and water-temperature survey data into a unified argument about fleet behavior under season consolidation. R40 (dense 0.895) uses NHTSA's own study data (15-second, 18.6-second, 20-second capture rates) to justify the specific recording-period proposal. Dense-low R24 cites part numbers and compliance months but draws no analytical conclusion beyond 'give us more time,' and R35 asserts 'substantial' economic impact without any quantification.

proposals.name: Implementation feasibility gap identification
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies specific actors, systems, or processes that the proposed rule depends on but that are unprepared, untrained, under-resourced, or unable to carry out their assigned role under the rule. A 10 means a specific actor, a specific gap, and a specific operational consequence are all named. A 0 means no implementation analysis is offered.
proposals.rationale: R33 (dense 0.636) asks exactly who will train USAF providers to conduct screenings they have never performed, identifying a concrete personnel-readiness gap. R36 (dense 0.789) identifies that FEMA staff lack familiarity with land-grant resource-use patterns, meaning sole-proprietor businesses will go unrecognized. Dense-low R58 raises FEMA review timelines but never specifies which actors cannot meet them or what operational breakdown results, which the dense model appears to discount.

proposals.name: Self-contained substantive completeness
proposals.instruction: Score whether the key analytical content of the comment can be fully understood and evaluated from the text of the comment itself, without requiring the reader to access attachments, confidential documents, or external materials for the substance. A 10 means every major argument is present and developed within the comment text. A 0 means the comment is essentially a cover letter or pointer to external materials, with little or no substance in the text itself.
proposals.rationale: R44 (dense 0.916) notes a PDF attachment but develops all key arguments—including the vegetable-seed count-vs-weight problem—within the comment text itself. R40 presents its complete EDR analysis in-text. Dense-low R04 ('Please see the attached comments from SIFMA'), R05 ('Please see the attached comments'), and R34 ('see attached PDF') are all cover letters whose substance is invisible to a text-only reader, which the dense model appears to penalize heavily even though the scorecard rewards them.

proposals.name: Statutory and legal reasoning quality
proposals.instruction: Score the quality of the comment's legal argument: whether it identifies the correct statutory or regulatory provision, explains the chain of legal reasoning step by step, and applies the law to the specific facts of the proposed action—not merely citing a statute or case name. A 10 means a self-contained, logically rigorous legal argument that a reviewer could follow and evaluate. A 0 means no legal argument, or a bare citation with no reasoning.
proposals.rationale: R02 and R32 (both dense-high versions of the same argument) explain the 110(k)(6) error-correction provision, walk through why EPA's prior removal was unlawful, and apply the provision to the reinstatement. R47 (dense 0.902) analyzes the CAA source-category definition to argue transmission-and-storage sources were improperly aggregated. Dense-low R57 cites PUD v. Washington Department of Ecology but does not develop the legal chain beyond restating the holding, and R13 invokes case law in service of a self-interested argument without independent legal analysis.

proposals.name: Argument-to-background density ratio
proposals.instruction: Score the proportion of the comment's substantive text devoted to advancing specific, novel regulatory arguments versus providing general background, context-setting, literature review, or restating what the proposed rule already says. A 10 means nearly every sentence advances a specific argument, objection, or recommendation that a regulator could act on. A 0 means nearly all text is background or context that an agency reviewer would already know.
proposals.rationale: R50 (dense 0.857) devotes every sentence to weighing costs and benefits for manufacturers, vendors, and consumers—zero background padding. R16 builds a concise causal argument in a few paragraphs. Dense-low R03 runs an extended academic essay on contractor casualties with minimal regulatory recommendation, R09 devotes pages to ecological description of tallgrass prairie before brief regulatory points, and R43 offers extensive background on wildlife corridors that a wildlife biologist at the agency would already know.

proposals.name: Stakeholder distributional mapping
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies specific groups affected by the rule and analyzes how costs, benefits, or risks distribute asymmetrically across them—showing who gains, who loses, and through what mechanism. A 10 means multiple distinct groups are identified with specific distributional consequences traced for each. A 0 means no distributional analysis, or all stakeholders are treated as an undifferentiated mass.
proposals.rationale: R08 maps the distributional consequences across small vape businesses, Big Tobacco companies, and adult consumers seeking harm-reduction alternatives. R16 traces how a dealer trust would shift costs across livestock sellers, dealers, and lenders with each link specified. R52 (dense 0.687) identifies communities with lead pipes, children in older housing, and industrial neighbors as distinct exposure groups. Dense-low R35 mentions for-hire operators and local businesses but does not analyze the distributional mechanism connecting them.

proposals.name: Counterexample to rule's foundational assumption
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment provides a specific real-world case, scenario, or empirical example that directly contradicts a foundational assumption underlying the proposed rule—showing that the premise on which the rule rests does not hold. A 10 means a concrete, documented counterexample that targets a specific premise. A 0 means no counterexample, or only a hypothetical that is not grounded in facts.
proposals.rationale: R16 (dense 0.652) uses the Sam Kane Beef Processors bankruptcy—where a Packers Trust was in place yet sellers still went unpaid—to demolish the premise that a trust reliably protects sellers. R38 cites 2020 acoustic-survey water-temperature data (2.7°C vs. 40-year average of 3.7°C) to counter the claim that roe-quality changes are a permanent trend justifying season consolidation. R30 (dense 0.902) uses EPA's own cost analysis to show that projected savings are negligible after accounting for increased leak costs.

proposals.name: Cross-regulatory coherence analysis
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment examines how the proposed rule interacts with other existing regulations, statutes, court decisions, or administrative processes, and explains whether the interaction creates harmony, redundancy, or conflict. A 10 means specific cross-references are identified with a clear analysis of coherence or tension. A 0 means no cross-regulatory analysis.
proposals.rationale: R02/R32 analyze how the Air Nuisance Rule fits within the broader SIP framework and the 110(k)(6) error-correction mechanism. R47 examines how combining transmission-and-storage with production sources under a single CAA source category creates an internally inconsistent regulatory structure. Dense-low R57 references a Supreme Court case but does not develop the analysis of how the proposed rule coheres or conflicts with the broader CWA Section 401 framework beyond a bare assertion.

proposals.name: Specificity and actionability of regulatory request
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment makes a clear, specific, and actionable request of the agency—exactly what should be changed, added, delayed, or reconsidered, with defined scope—rather than a general expression of support or opposition. A 10 means the request is precise enough that an agency drafter could act on it directly (e.g., 'extend comment period to March 1, 2022' or 'require 20 seconds of pre-crash data at 10 Hz'). A 0 means only a vague position like 'I support' or 'I oppose' with no actionable content.
proposals.rationale: R51 requests a specific extension date (March 1, 2022) and specific policy actions (delay quota distribution, require Charter Headboat proof). R52 demands specific commitments: lower acceptable lead levels for paint, and mandatory replacement timelines for lead pipes. R40 endorses a specific 20-second / 10-Hz standard with evidentiary justification. Dense-low R11 opposes SOE removal without specifying any alternative regulatory path, and R10 asks for parity with solid-organ reimbursement without any mechanism or threshold.

proposals.name: Forward-looking problem anticipation
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a specific problem, risk, or scenario that the proposed rule does not address but that is likely to arise if the rule is adopted as written—showing the agency something it has not yet considered. A 10 means a novel, specific, and well-reasoned problem that the rule's text does not contemplate. A 0 means no forward-looking analysis, or only generic warnings like 'this could be problematic.'
proposals.rationale: R33 (dense 0.636) anticipates that centralizing the dependent-screening process will leave USAF providers—who have never conducted these screenings—without training or clear referral pathways. R08 anticipates that the PMTA process will functionally transfer the entire ENDS market to Big Tobacco. R29 (dense 0.769) anticipates national-security risks from public exposure of classified repository data. Dense-low R59 asserts offshore wind 'should be banned' but does not articulate a specific scenario the harvest-specifications rule fails to address.

proposals.name: Evidence-to-conclusion logical transparency
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment's reasoning is explicit and traceable: a reader can follow each step from evidence to inference to conclusion, and the comment distinguishes clearly between facts, analytical inferences, and value judgments. A 10 means the logical architecture is fully visible—premises are stated, inferences are labeled, and the conclusion follows necessarily. A 0 means conclusions are asserted with no visible reasoning chain.
proposals.rationale: R40 lays out the study methodology, then the specific findings (15 seconds captures 50% of intersection events, 18.6 seconds captures 90%, 20 seconds captures 99%), then the policy conclusion—a fully transparent chain. R44 presents each comment as: proposed text → problem identified → recommended revision → rationale, a model of logical transparency. Dense-low R59 jumps from a quote about offshore wind environmental effects to the conclusion 'should be banned' with no intermediate reasoning, and R53 asserts that non-PMR physicians 'provide excellent care' without any visible evidence-to-conclusion chain.

proposals.name: Practical operational knowledge depth
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment demonstrates detailed, fine-grained knowledge of how the regulated activity actually works on the ground—knowledge that reveals operational realities the rule does not account for. This is about the depth and specificity of practical understanding, whether from direct experience or professional expertise. A 10 means the operational knowledge is detailed enough to expose specific gaps in the rule's understanding of the activity it regulates. A 0 means the comment displays no operational knowledge beyond what the proposed rule itself states.
proposals.rationale: R38 reveals the existence of voluntary fleet stand-down agreements, their dependence on small fleet size, and their role in controlling Chinook bycatch—operational knowledge absent from the agency's analysis. R07 explains screen-brightness controls and non-backing driving scenarios that the rule's timeout logic ignores. R51 (dense 0.835) explains the practical reality of the 'Wicked Tuna effect' and how the fishery has evolved into a part-time tourist activity the agency does not account for. Dense-low R53 and R59 display no operational knowledge of the activities they address.

proposals.name: Plain conversational register vs. formal/technical prose
proposals.instruction: Read the comment's sentence structure and vocabulary only (ignore whether its claims are correct). Score 10 if the writing reads like ordinary spoken conversation: short simple sentences, everyday vocabulary, few or no multi-clause legal/technical constructions, no defined terms or outline numbering. Score 0 if the writing is dense formal/technical prose: long multi-clause sentences, specialized vocabulary, defined terms, or outline/section numbering (I., A., 1.). Score in between for a mix of the two registers.
proposals.rationale: Plainly-worded conversational comments cluster in dense_high_card_low even when their claims are thin, e.g. R04 ('Its important for many consumers who have health issues...') and R30 ('Hello! I sincerely hope that Boutique Air will continue...'), both dense_high_card_low (.857, .567), versus the outline-numbered technical register of comments like R34 and R39. We expect the dense model to reward easy-to-parse conversational cadence independent of whether the underlying claim is substantiated.
proposals.upstream_parent: surface-only

proposals.name: Verbatim or template-matched cross-submission duplication
proposals.instruction: Judge only from the single comment text (no access to other comments).
